# Cross-provider routing inputs

Use each as a read-only instruction case; no live model dispatch or external
write. A coordinator's task already authorizes ordinary independent review, with
Standards and Specification required. All current comparison and acceptance
sources are supplied unless the case says otherwise. Do not inspect the separate
expectations until returning the independent routing decisions.

## CP01: Routine change
Low impact, bounded correction, no unresolved dispute, qualified native reviewers.

## CP02: High-impact gate
A small change controls permission to merge. Both providers have qualified paths
and suitable reviewers meeting the current impact floor. The substantive risk is
an incorrect Standards/security decision. Two final independent axes are required.

## CP03: Substantive disagreement
Specification and implementation disagree whether a missing required check can be
ignored. This is unresolved correctness/evidence, not wording. A qualified other
provider can cover the Specification axis. A current blocking finding is open.

## CP04: Cosmetic disagreement
Two readers prefer different heading capitalization. The requirement permits both.
The low-impact change has no unresolved correctness question.

## CP05: Other provider unavailable
High-impact change, no qualified other-provider path. Two eligible independent
native reviewers satisfy every ordinary required axis/control for the current
comparison. No explicit owner requirement names the unavailable provider.

## CP06: Mandatory restriction unavailable
The coordinator is on Claude. Its project mandates verified restricted reviewer
tools. Native reviewer tool restrictions cannot be verified and the separate
process path is not qualified. Someone suggests unrestricted Claude fallback.

## CP07: Owner-selected provider/settings
High-impact change. The owner explicitly requires Codex Standards on Astra at
high and Codex Specification on Sol at high. A qualified Claude path also exists.

## CP08: Partial or stale diversity
An other-provider reviewer returns only a general summary, without required axis
coverage. Another return covered the previous head. Native required coverage is
not yet complete. The coordinator has a successful launch receipt for each.

## CP09: Resume and changed input
After interruption, the coordinator has retained provider, settings, finding IDs,
actual returns and allowances. The head changes only a documented subarea. It
proposes resetting round counts and launching two complete teams automatically.

## CP10: Provider shopping
A qualified review raised an unresolved blocking finding. Another provider is
unavailable. A round limit is exhausted and the coordinator wants to repeat
providers until an approval appears.

## CP11: Focused uncovered question
A high-impact change also has a specialist concurrency question that the two
required axis briefs cannot cover with their current qualified reviewers. One
qualified other-provider specialist can cover the concurrency question only.
